claims.content: When the Customer attempts to cancel a confirmed bid, the system blocks the retraction because auction bids may not be cancelled. Cancelling is considered unfair and unethical (preventing shill bidding). If the cancelled bid would have been the winning bid, the system does not automatically award the item to the next person in line because it has no way to follow up to notify or offer second-place finishers.

claims.content: The Customer triggers the use case by canceling a bid during an auction.
The cancelled bid is removed from the auction's active bidding record and from consideration as a winning bid.
If the cancelled bid was the highest bid, the next person in line would theoretically become the winner.
The Customer has a confirmed bid in the auction.
The auction is in progress at the time of retraction.
The Customer wants to cancel/retract their own bid during an auction.

When the Customer attempts to cancel a confirmed bid, the system blocks the retraction because auction bids may not be cancelled. Cancelling is considered unfair and unethical (preventing shill bidding). If the cancelled bid would have been the winning bid, the system does not automatically award the item to the next person in line because it has no way to follow up to notify or offer second-place finishers.
